notes.title: Ferulorum(V-1.1.14) Steam Release
notes.notes:
Consider buying the game being a donation lol

I've included an image of the shire in this upload hopefully to convey my feeling of reaching the end of a long, unexpected journey. I was expecting the making of this game to be much faster because from the beginning it was mostly meant to be a project to get better at c++ and get over the fear of putting something on steam, and while it was never going to be technically impressive or a smash hit I just couldn't bring myself to call it done while it was even rougher than it is now (god is it rough). But as you can tell by the title the time has come, I sat with my finger over the publish button on steam for a long time and to be honest I think I basically had stage fright, but it had to be done my old bad code and poor game design decisions have made it so I'm basically backed into a corner as to improve the game would take huge code changes and probably changing the game on a fundamental level. That is not to say I hate this project I am extremely proud of making it to the finish line and the blood and sweat I put into it but I know this isn't a game people will love its just missing that core thing that a good game needs  and my ability to keep focusing on just the same thing is at its absolute limits. 

This week I made some good progress filled out the game with some more content and variety and fixed lots of small issues, specifically every item is now in the game and the hero's now have a lot more options. I also started tweaking some of the Ui to try and make it more readable.

In the coming weeks the plan is to continue working on ferulorum and fixing the last of its small issues and also to transition gradually into my next project.  I've actually already started  what I'm calling Chamoisee-Canvasback (just a stand in code name) by setting up the project file and downloading the library's I'm planning on using SDL3.

Im also going to wait about a month to do a post mortem but the long and short of it will be that ferulorum was a big success and the biggest lesson from it is that the decisions I make early in a project will come back to haunt me later on in a project.

So that's it for this one It was a pretty good week hopefully next week is even better for everyone and hopefully my next project will be at least 2x as good as this one.

notes.title: Ferulorum(V-0.1.12) Steam & Faltering
notes.notes:
This week was my least productive week yet, a total failed week (mission failed we'll get them next time) .  Constant distractions have taken their toll both in the form of people, sleep issues, general tiredness, and that fact I have now gotten into 40k. after about a year of basically dopamine fasting getting into tabletop gaming is basically heroin for my caveman brain (I've included pics of some of my boys), I haven't actually played yet just bult the models and started priming. I've avoided this for a long time because I knew I would get addicted and because games workshop has done a lot of things that made me mad but my cousin dragged me in, I also wanted to try to spend as little money as possible so I bought a starter set that was like $100 but I needed some more models to complete my army and just the 3 guys with shells were $80 dollars.  So I have now been fighting the urge to by a 3d printer.

It was not all bad news this week I managed to get my demo and game approved by steam and the demo is live but for the most part all I managed to do this week was work on balancing the game :(      I'm also building out my library of song ideas.

For next week the save system needs to be finished no matter what .

Project Chamoisee-Canvasback planning has continued I think I have it clearly formed in my mind how I want it to look and feel.

This week is has given me another reason to be more discerning with how far I develop my next project because it would be a lot easier to work on all this boring stuff and maintain my willpower if I new I was working on something people would love, opening my project right now is the opposite of the beginning of the project nothing new to learn or fun challenges to solve just drudge work.

So it was a bad week but that water is under the bridge so hopefully next week goes better see you all next time.

notes.title: Ferulorum(V-0.1.10) Demo & Destruction
notes.notes:
This update has destruction in its title because daylight savings time has destroyed the schedule I was on and I blaming it for what was possibly my worst week over the course of this project, I've included a squidward picture as a representation of how daylight savings has affected me.

As I said in the last paragraph the progress for this week was not good (I also did roof work this week leaving me extra tired) I fixed some bugs and did some work on balance, the biggest improvement was probably in choosing the ambient sounds for the last levels. I spent a lot of time  trying to find sounds that fit the vibe I wanted But once I downloaded 14,000 presets for synth1 it became super easy to find what I wanted. In other news I've also started preparing to launch both my demo and full game on steam this is truly the end stage of this project.

For the week a head I think the only things left to work on are the end game, the save system, and balance and maybe add in some more items (super easy to do) and that's really all there is.

I have started slowly gearing up for my next project code name Chamoisee-Canvasback, I've mostly just came up with the cool codename and made an empty visual studio project. But I've also started the slow buildup of making the design document for it Ill probably reveal what I'm doing more as I wrap up ferulorum to try and smoothly move from one to the next, so the only hint ill give is that im taking a game I liked a long time ago and a mechanic from a recently made game and combining them.

So that's all for this one hope you all had a good week and hopefully next week is even better.

notes.title: Ferulorum(V-0.1.09) Intro wow!
notes.notes:
I went to a game dinner this week it hamstrung progress for two days but I found out alligator taste good!

This week I believe I finished the sound effects and I also made an intro that just needs a few more adjustments before being finished, as usual I also spent a bunch of time working on fixing bugs and trying to balance the game.  I fell a little short of my goals in terms of working on the save system mostly because I know its going to be painful to do - but I know what I have to do so finishing it should only take one day if I put my nose to the grindstone.

For the week ahead I'm planning on fleshing out the leveling system, the game over screen and end credits, the save system, fixing bugs and balance.

Things truly are wrapping up if things feel good I might try to put a demo up on steam and maybe two weeks from now ill release on steam in early access. If been doing kind of short thoughts on the mistakes I've made on this project and one I was thinking about today was about my use of functions. If you are not a programmer a function is just a neat little package that lets you reuse code without having to type it out again, so because of the way a structured the project I avoided using large amount of functions out of fear that it would lead to a confusing  mess but I was looking at some of my code today and I was just hit the realization that I'm an idiot. I definitely should have used a lot more of them especially now that I'm better at c++ and just moving around code in general.

Thats it for this one it wasn't a bad week considering how many distractions there were so hopefully you all had a good week, and hopefully next week is even better.

notes.title: Ferulorum(V-0.1.08) Sound
notes.notes:
Added the steam page to the itch page no idea where it will show up may keep adding the link hear depending on where it shows up.

This week instead of a meme I've added a nice quote about dreams, I always see devs online talking about their dream games I don't know if I have a dream game I think I have around 200 game ideas written down I feel like my dream is just to be great at something and win (I've only ever won participation trophy's).

So this week I spent lots of time making sound effects like I planned on, sound effects are an interesting challenge because no one notices them but they can completely change the feeling of a game. To be honest I think I might have a latent talent for being bad at making them lmao so based on the feedback I get I might just replace them with for free sounds online, like what does a knight protecting his friend sound like? - they are fun to make though. I was also planning on working on the end game but never got to it as playtesting is still taking a long time and there's so many bugs its like I'm worm charming as I move around the code.

For the week coming up the end game, sound effects and the save system will be my main targets there is also a game jam coming up for the developer community a follow that is always fun to do.

I've also made a decision for my next game as I think about the lessons that I have learned with Ferulorum and that is I'm going to make one level, one player character, one enemy, and no graphics until it's fun and if it's not I'll change whatever I need to for fun to be achieved.

That's all for this one hope you all had a good week and hopefully the next one is even better.

notes.title: Ferulorum(V-0.1.06) Final Leg
notes.notes:
I've included a picture of Hisoka eating his own arm in this update  to reflect my mental state (this is tradition now) I'm eager for what lies ahead I don't think Ferulorum will get and sales (one good review would blow away expectations) but something about approaching the finish line and knowing all the things I want to do next and all the skills /knowledge I've gained has me hungry.

This week's progress was neither good nor bad unfortunately there were a lot of distractions, but I still managed to get some stuff done, I fixed lots of bugs, worked on the stockpile, made good progress on the shop, added all the hero's alternate sprites, started working on the level up system and worked on the save system a little. 

Right now the game is probably 90%  done  yet the final leg of this race is really stretching many of the mistakes I've made earlier on are taking their tole, some of them programming related but I'm also being punished for poor game design decisions that I made. The main one being balancing the dungeons, on my next project one thing is certain there will only be one enemy and one player class until all of the other systems have been completed because trying to figure out a way to make it so that 12 hero classes can get through five dungeons in a fair but challenging way while also having lots of random generation is hampering progress greatly, and while I'm doing my best I think this might be unfixable completely at this point.

So on that note next week will be all about balance, polish, bug fixing, sound effects, player qol, and tying up loose ends in systems. Since all the major stuff is done things will be pretty boring for the rest of this project as far as I can tell, all I can do is try my best and hope a few people appreciate what I've created.

So I hope you all had a good week and hope next week is even better for whatever reason I'm optimistic right now (rare!)

notes.title: Ferulorum(V-0.1.05) Shop & Save
notes.notes:
Another week down and I would rate this one 8/10 not a perfect week but one with good consistent progress. Last week I had some trouble with saving and while my solution is not pretty its one that works and I can use with lots of confidence along with this the shop is basically done (wow). it actually wasn't to hard to implement I just kind of grafted it onto the item and stockpile code which is a nice change of pace due to these systems being newer and reworked, If these had been done at the beginning of the project like hero's I would have had to redo a lot of stuff (I have improved). 

Including a picture of Patric star to represent my mental state again.

In the week ahead the plan is to tackle hero leveling and balance and hopefully put together a demo,  I don't want to jinx it but I think it is all green fields ahead. I don't have plans to add any further functionality that I haven't done before so all that's left is making the game as fun, interactable, understandable, and satisfying as possible. notes.title: Ferulorum(V-0.1.0) Beta
notes.notes:
Officially in beta, what does that mean exactly? I'm starting to actually make the game fun and worry about user experience. 

So my two big concerns right now are getting the player to understand what is happening and to also allow them to make decisions that can change the outcome of dungeon runs, also I'm trying to make stuff more juicy and interactive.

And right now  I'm trying to implement a message system that will tell the player what has happened and also guide them to the next step, so as an example when you start the game there's a message talking about the tavern hopefully this leads to players clicking on the tavern. Along with this I'm going to make it so that more relevant menus pop open like when you click on a hero to hire the deep info panel will pop open (right now hiring hero opens no menu so people hire one and it seems like nothing has happened).

As far as decision making goes I want the main challenge of the game to be putting together the right hero teams for dungeon runs using the random hero's they have available. I think part of this is solved through the dungeon combat log but also I need to find a way to show more info to the player and I'm not sure how yet. I think items will also be an important part of player decisions and I might work on that this week,

For making  the game feel better I have one main idea and that is making the enemy's much weaker so that the hero team kills more of them and having them explode when they die. I think in general making the game feel good is not a hard thing to figure out (make every player action have a reaction so the game feels tactile and alive) but it seems like it will be daunting.

Over all this week blew by I was sick, tired, there was a holiday I think, I was in a game jam for demos where I got some good feedback (that my game is broke and confusing) , and I made some good progress despite that. So all in all not bad

Hopefully this week is good and all of us  keep on trucking !

notes.title: Ferulorum(V-0.0.8) Combat
notes.notes:
Ok so it was a pretty good week I made major improvement to the combat system making it so armor actually block damage, and all the heroes have ability's that hopefully make team building much more strategic and fun, I've also made it so that enemy's and heroes have the ability to miss and dodge.

the game is quickly approaching what I would call beta if this week goes good then ill consider announcing it officially and putting together a demo.

in this upcoming week I want to take my first pass at adding juice to the game, my plan is to try to make combat have a lot of particle effects (started particle system today) and also have messages telling the player everything that's happening and damage numbers everywhere. I also have to do another pass over combat and make sure hero stats effect all the stuff that's happening.

in this post I'm including pics of all the steam art assets I've made (which I'm actually pretty proud of) as well as some enemy flavor text since I've finished all of it.

hopefully all of you had a good week and another good one this week!
